title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three lines of title on a flush-left margin, a process-red running time, one heavy brass rule under the title, the writer's credit on the margin at the forme's foot, the colophon hung on the figure's edge. Each title line breaks only at a join, a word space or one break inside a long word, and the sorts either side stay locked up on one baseline. Push a line down and it breaks a whole tread, the title's x-height: flat treads, hard risers. Push harder and the push passes down the stack, the next line breaks, then the next, one tread a push, until the title is three stairs stacked to the foot of the forme; a line shoved from above goes down whole on the margin. The rule is one length of brass and only moves whole: the moment a letter comes down into it, it drops in one knock to the foot of the forme, its face as heavy as the figures' stems and centred on the red's baseline, so the figures stand on the brass and their feet print a third, darker ink.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
